title: The Mechanics of Pre-suasion: Causes, Constraints, and Correctives
coreMove: Test whether a prepared concept is truly relevant, temporary, and correctable before relying on it.
sourcePressure: The source explains mechanisms, constraints, and correctives: concepts fire when readied, not only when ready, and pre-suasion has limits rather than magical force.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Priming lets you plant any idea and make it work.

hook: An abstract claim that attention changes everything
A generic meeting where someone makes a better pitch
A clever sentence about persuasion before any concrete object appears
counterintuition: You think persuasion happens during the ask, but it happens before it
The obvious factor is not always the important one
Influence is not manipulation when used well
tryThisNow: Set a timer and reflect on attention
Write down three ways to be more persuasive
Ask yourself what matters most right now

exampleSpecs.audience: a nurse manager checking whether a pain-scale prompt readies the wrong concern
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a prepared concept helps or distorts the next answer
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager compares responses when insurance questions come before versus after symptom sorting
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a triage tablet paused on the insurance screen

exampleSpecs.audience: a court administrator testing whether early questions bias later fairness ratings
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether readied concepts can be corrected by order changes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the administrator moves neighborhood questions after evidence instructions and tracks what changes
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a questionnaire packet with reordered tabs

exampleSpecs.audience: a bank compliance officer limiting priming by debt language
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether callers are readied for shame before hearing options
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the officer replaces the opening balance recitation with a neutral identity check and compares take-up
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a call script with the balance line struck through

exampleSpecs.audience: an exhibit designer showing uncertainty without making guesses feel like facts
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether readied curiosity stays inside evidence limits
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the designer adds a correction label beside the mystery prompt before visitors press the answer button
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an exhibit button glowing under a question panel

exampleSpecs.audience: a menu owner testing if health icons crowd out taste decisions too strongly
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a cue’s reach exceeds the decision it should inform
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the owner checks whether diners avoid balanced dishes with one red icon before changing the icon system
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a menu proof with red icons beside three entrees

exampleSpecs.audience: an HR analyst preventing one word from contaminating all answers
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether readied resentment spreads beyond the target issue
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the analyst removes the word complaint from the opener and adds a later corrective item
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a survey preview with the first prompt highlighted

skillTargets: explain readied concepts without treating them as control
detect spillover from an early cue
revise order when a prime contaminates later judgment

tryThisNowSpec: Find one early cue in a form, script, or meeting and ask what concept it readies, what it might distort, and what correction belongs nearby.
